We need to implement solution for problem: given array batteryPercentages length n (0-indexed). For i from 0..n-1: if batteryPercentages[i] > 0: increment count (tested devices). Then for all j from i+1 to n-1: batteryPercentages[j] = max(0, batteryPercentages[j] - 1). Continue.

Goal: return number of tested devices after processing all i in order.

Constraints: n up to 100, values up to 100; simple O(n^2) simulation works.

But there might be more efficient solution: count of positive after subtracting number of previously tested devices? Since each time we test a device at index i, we decrement all later devices by 1. So batteryPercentages[j] gets decreased by number of tests performed before j (i.e., number of indices i < j where batteryPercentages[i] > 0 after previous reductions?). Actually we test a device i only if its current value after previous decrements >0. At time of testing i, its value = original batteryPercentages[i] - number_of_previously_tested_devices_before_i (since each previous test decrements all later devices, including i) but not below 0. So we can compute count as number of i where batteryPercentages[i] - tested_so_far > 0. Because each test increments tested_so_far (cnt) and reduces all later by 1. So we can just simulate with a variable tested = 0; for each value v in batteryPercentages: if v - tested > 0: tested += 1. Finally return tested. That's O(n). Actually we must ensure not to go below zero; but condition v - tested > 0 is enough, because if v - tested <=0 then battery is zero or negative after previous decrements, so we skip.

Check with examples: [1,1,2,1,3]; tested=0; v=1 => 1-0>0 -> tested=1; v=1 =>1-1=0 not >0 -> skip; v=2=>2-1=1>0 -> tested=2; v=1=>1-2=-1 not >0 -> skip; v=3=>3-2=1>0 -> tested=3 => answer 3 matches.
